name: Cheniere Energy
description: Cheniere buys US natural gas, cools it into liquid (LNG) at two huge Gulf Coast export plants (Sabine Pass, Louisiana and Corpus Christi, Texas) and ships it to buyers around the world. It says it is the largest US LNG producer and second largest LNG operator worldwide by liquefaction capacity, with over 60 million tonnes a year including projects under construction. Its model is closer to a tolling fee than a bet on gas prices: about three quarters of LNG revenue comes from long-term contracts where customers pay a fixed fee per MMBtu whether or not they take cargoes, plus a variable charge tied to 115% of the US gas benchmark; the rest is sold by its own marketing arm at market prices. 2025 revenue was 19,976 million dollars and net income attributable to Cheniere 5,330 million (3,252 million in 2024). GAAP quarterly results can swing widely: a 3.5 billion dollar loss in Q1 2026 was followed by 3,068 million of profit in Q2 2026, leaving a 434 million dollar loss for the half (cause of the swings not extracted). It returns cash through a growing dividend and buybacks, with a 10 billion dollar repurchase authority for 2026 to 2030.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. SEC SIC code 4924 (Natural Gas Distribution). Cheniere is closer to a tolling business for gas than to a pipeline or a producer.

hq.note: City and state from the EDGAR submissions record

employees.note: Full-time employees, 1,617 in the US and 100 outside (mainly UK); FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: LNG sold under third-party long-term agreements
businessLines.how: Customers pay a fixed liquefaction fee per MMBtu whether or not they lift cargoes, plus a variable fee equal to a percentage of the US gas benchmark; the company aims to contract about 90% of capacity this way, making earnings largely insensitive to LNG prices.
businessLines.description: LNG from the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi plants sold to utilities, portfolio players and national companies under long-term sale and purchase agreements (SPAs).
businessLines.marketShare: Company says it is the largest US LNG producer and second-largest LNG operator globally by capacity (FY2025 10-K); rivals' capacities not extracted

businessLines.name: LNG sold by Cheniere Marketing (short-term and spot)
businessLines.how: Sells cargoes at market-linked prices; earns a margin over the gas cost and shipping, so this is the price-sensitive part of the business.
businessLines.description: Uncontracted LNG from the plants plus cargoes procured from third parties, sold on the global market.

revenue.note: Plus 226 million from LNG procured from third parties and 344 million net derivative gain; 2024: 2,345 short-term

businessLines.revenueNote: Plus 226 million from LNG procured from third parties and 344 million net derivative gain; 2024: 2,345 short-term

businessLines.name: Regasification and other
businessLines.how: Fee from a customer that holds regasification capacity, plus miscellaneous.
businessLines.description: Sabine Pass regasification capacity, plus other revenues (405 million dollars in 2025) and other LNG revenue items (267 million).

brands.name: Sabine Pass Liquefaction (SPL), Louisiana
brands.share: Over 30 mtpa of production capacity, about half of the over 60 mtpa total (computed); one of the largest LNG facilities in the world; SPL Expansion Project pre-FID

brands.name: Corpus Christi Liquefaction (CCL), Texas
brands.share: Over 30 mtpa expected including over 9 mtpa under construction at Dec 31, 2025; Stage 3 is seven midscale Trains adding over 10 mtpa; Midscale Trains 8 and 9 add about 5 mtpa

brands.name: Cheniere Energy Partners (CQP)
brands.segment: Publicly traded subsidiary that owns the Sabine Pass business
brands.share: Net income attributable to non-controlling interests 1,464 million dollars of 6,794 million dollars net income in 2025, about 22% (computed), showing how much profit belongs to CQP's outside unitholders

whatsNext.text: Corpus Christi Stage 3: six of seven midscale trains in operation by Q2 2026 with about 1 mtpa still under construction; two further midscale Trains 8 and 9 (about 5 mtpa) planned

SPL Expansion Project (phased, FERC application updated June 2025) and CCL expansion: phased final investment decisions still pending; DOE free-trade export authorization of 950 Bcf per year granted Nov 2025 for SPL Expansion
